[[File:Clan Wars logo.png|left]]
'''Clan Wars''' is a safe [[minigame]] located in [[Ferox Enclave]], in a safe area of the Wilderness.

Clan Wars allows members of two opposing [[chat-channel]]s to engage in player-versus-player combat against one another. A white [[free-for-all portal]] is available in addition to the normal ones. This portal is used by players to practice, to have fun in a PvP zone, or to restore drained stats and [[Hitpoints]] upon exiting.

The purple portals are often used by [[Clans|PvP Clans]] to practice among their members or to fight against other clans. It is seldom used by casual clans. Instead, the free-for-all white portal is more popular.

==Transportation==
There are three safe methods of reaching Ferox Enclave that does not require players to traverse the Wilderness:
* A [[ring of dueling]] (Ferox Enclave) will teleport directly here.
* Using [[Minigame Teleport]] either through the spellbook or the [[Grouping]] interface to teleport to the Clan Wars minigame.
* Using a [[waka canoe]] to row here (requires level 57 [[Woodcutting]]).

==Setting up a clan fight==
A clan fight may be setup by [[chat-channel]] members who are ranked a captain or higher by using the "Challenge" [[Choose Option|option]] on a player from another chat-channel (chat-channel was referred to as "Clan Chat" during release; it is not to be confused with the similar [[clan]] system). When challenging another clan, leaders may customise the terms and conditions for winning. Once the leaders have agreed, the minigame will begin. Clanmates will be notified in the chat-channel that a war has begun and can enter the purple portal. There will be a two-minute timer and a wall separating clans. At the end of the two-minute timer, the walls will collapse and the battle will begin.

Players who die will be sent to a jail where depending on the game option, can go back in or will be unable to fight again. There is also an option to watch the fight at any time via orbs scattered across the map.

==Purple Portal Arenas==
To join a fight, players must be in a [[chat-channel]], and a ranking member that is captain or higher must initiate a war with another chat-channel. When the war has been initiated, players have 2 minutes to enter the arena before the war starts. Depending on the settings, once this 2 minute timer is up, players may or may not be able to enter the battle. There can only be a maximum of 100 players per side for a total of 200 players maximum.

There are a total of 12 maps that players can choose for the purple portal. Four of the maps are [[Member|members-only]]. Each map has certain advantages and disadvantages for teams and fighting styles. Below are the available maps for the purple portal arena.

===<span class="anchor" id="Purple Portal Strategies & Tactics"></span> Strategies and tactics===

[[File:Falling in Clan Wars.png|thumb|250x250px|A clan falling in on their leader at the start of the battle.]]

====Falling in====
A popular strategy in F2P fights is falling in. At the beginning of the war and throughout the war, a member of the clan types "fall in" and everybody follows this person into battle. The fall in leader's job is to keep everyone organized and together so that everyone is going to the same place. This is a tactic commonly utilised in F2P fights but rarely in P2P fights. One reason for this is because in members worlds, barraging is common so if everyone is together, this makes it easier for the opposing team to ice barrage a huge amount of players.

[[File:Piling Clan Wars.png|thumb|250x250px|A clan piling an unfortunate member of the opposing team.]]

====Piling====
Piling is when multiple people on your team are attacking one opponent. This is also a common tactic utilised in F2P PvP scenarios because if you have more people attacking your opponent, the faster it will be to kill them. If you have enough players targeting an opposing player, and their [[Defence]] level is also low, you may be able to kill them faster than they are able to heal themselves with food. Clan leaders often utilise this tactic by calling out the name of an opponent to pile next, either through voice chat or through in game chat.

[[File:Camping Clan Wars.png|thumb|Players camping on this turret during a game of Clan Wars]]

====Camping or DDing====
This is also a common strategy in F2P wars and occasionally P2P as well. One team goes to a certain area on the map and camps there and waits for the opposing team to come to them. This is commonly utilised on the turrets map as the castles throughout the arena can be used to range or mage at incoming enemies. One advantage to this strategy is that it makes it easier for everyone on your team to stick together in one spot. The disadvantage is that if the opposing clan manages to trap or overwhelm you, then it's harder to recover from. 

====Freezing or snaring====
Magic is very important in team PvP situations in both free to play and pay to play. This is why using spells to freeze your opponent in place is very common in most battles. In P2P, mages have access to ice barrage which prevents enemy players from moving. Against opponents who are only using melee, ice barrage is a very effective strategy against them as it neutralizes their ability to fight back.

In free to play wars, magic is also very important and frequently used. F2P mages have access to snare which is a spell that freezes an opponent for 10 seconds. Snare is very important in F2P wars as it can freeze people who are trying to run away, giving your team a new target to pile. The downside to maging in F2P worlds is having very poor defensive stats. To make up for this, many mages will also have rune armour in their inventory and quickly switch to wearing their rune armour if they are attacked by opposing players.

==Free-for-all==
{{Map|name=Clan wars free-for-all arena (location)|width=260|height=260|x=3328|y=4800|plane=0|zoom=1|mapID=-1|caption=The free-for-all arena|align=right}}
In addition to the purple portals, there is also a [[free-for-all portal]] west of the bank area. Players will be able to recognise it by its white colour. Unlike the purple portals, there are no set teams or setting up fights between clans. Instead, it is a place where players can challenge each other one-on-one, or in [[multi-combat]] zones without having to worry about losing their items.

This portal is often used by players to restore drained stats (including [[Hitpoints]], [[Prayer]] and [[run energy]]) and cure [[poison]], as entering the portal and exiting it (via itself or a teleport) will restore stats and cure [[venom]] and poison.

The free-for-all portal is also a popular place for players to AFK train [[Magic]], especially in [[F2P]]. Two players wield armour, which makes their attacks always miss, start attacking each other and they go AFK. Since the fight never ends, and players get experience even if they miss, this is a decent way to train Magic.

A [[Mysterious Portal]] can be found in the south-eastern corner of the free-for-all arena. This portal was used by the participants of [[Deadman: All Stars Season 2]] to access the [[Deadman Arenas]] finale area.
